issues.legal_issue: A holder of only a life estate cannot transfer absolute title to the property.
material_facts: The original donor’s deed limited the interest of the donees and provided for devolution to their male legal heirs.
After the relevant male heir died, his widow held only a life estate in the property.
The widow sold the property, and the High Court treated her as its absolute owner without evidence or reasons for reversing the lower courts’ findings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in treating the widow as the absolute owner; she held only a life estate and could not convey absolute title by the sale.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of the deed and the concurrent findings established that the widow held only a life estate. The respondent’s counsel fairly conceded that a Hindu widow with only a life estate could not acquire absolute title. The Court relied on the absence of evidence or reasons supporting the High Court’s reversal of those findings; it did not undertake a wider determination of the disputed rules of French Hindu law.

predicates.civil_title_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning title to property.
predicates.property_interest_limited_to_life: The transferor held the property only for life under the governing instrument or succession.
predicates.unsupported_reversal_of_limited_interest: A reviewing court treated the transferor as having an absolute interest without evidence or reasons for overturning findings that the interest was limited.

issues.definition: When a property-title appeal concerns a transfer by a holder whose interest was limited to life, and a reviewing court has unsupportedly reversed that limitation, the transfer did not convey absolute title.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking a declaration of title must also seek possession when the defendants are in possession and able to deliver it.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought declarations of legal heirship and title, and that an earlier sale deed was void, but did not seek possession.
The defendants and their tenants were in possession of the property, and the defendants were in a position to deliver possession.
The defendants objected in their written statement to the omission of consequential relief, and the plaintiff did not amend the plaint to seek possession.

The lower appellate court considered that the plaintiff might seek eviction through separate proceedings, but the Supreme Court held that this would defeat the requirements against omitting consequential relief and multiplying proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not maintainable because the plaintiff sought only declaratory relief despite the defendants’ possession and did not seek the consequential relief of possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a plaintiff cannot seek a bare declaration when able to seek further consequential relief. A plaintiff must claim possession where defendants in possession can deliver it; reliance on later proceedings under another enactment does not avoid that requirement. The Court distinguished Deo Kuer v. Sheo Prasad Singh, where the defendants were not in physical possession and could not deliver possession, and applied Vinay Krishna v. Keshav Chandra, which required possession to be claimed where others were in possession. It also relied on the purpose of avoiding multiplicity of proceedings and on Muni Lal v. Oriental Fire & General Insurance Co. Ltd., which stated that omission of consequential relief requires refusal of declaratory relief.

rule.if: declaratory_title_suit and defendants_in_possession and defendants_can_deliver_possession and consequential_relief_omitted

predicates.declaratory_title_suit: The plaintiff brings a suit seeking a declaration of title to property.
predicates.defendants_in_possession: The defendants, including persons holding through them, are in possession of the property.
predicates.defendants_can_deliver_possession: The defendants in possession are in a position to deliver possession to the plaintiff.
predicates.consequential_relief_omitted: The plaintiff does not seek possession or other necessary consequential relief in the suit.

issues.definition: A suit seeking a declaration of title is not maintainable when the defendants are in possession and able to deliver possession if the plaintiff omits to seek that consequential relief.
